newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World rubber pact enters into force.
newsitem.headline: World rubber pact enters into force.

text.p: The 1995 International Natural Rubber Agreement entered into force on Thursday for a period of up to 12 months under a provisional pact by producers and consumers, UNCTAD chief Rubens Ricupero said. Ricupero, of the U.N. Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) which sponsored the negotiations in Geneva told a meeting: "It is therefore adopted. I see no objections."
P.O Thomas, speaking on behalf of the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO), based in Kuala-Lumpur, welcomed the entry into force of the delayed pact.

"It signifies the continued keen interest and concern of major natural rubber importers and exporters have in the operation of the international rubber pact, whose main objective is stabilisation of prices," he told the meeting.

The 1995 International Natural Rubber Agreement stipulates that it can only enter into force once ratified by 80 per cent of both exporting and importing countries. But they may agree on a temporary entry-into-force if the average is 75 per cent.

Some 97.3 per cent of producer countries have ratified the stymied pact, including the world's five biggest -- Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and Nigeria. Leading importers -- the United States, European Union and Japan -- have also ratified it but only 73.4 per cent of the importers have finalised their approval.
